x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Pulomavi III was defeated by the Ikshvaku Srisantamula and spent his last days at Myakadoni (Bellary). Statement 3 is wrong: he was the 30th and last king, one of the later Satavahanas (rulers 24-30), not the early group of rulers 1-23. So 1 and 2 only (A).

The Nigama Sabha, the urban council that administered towns, is referred to in the Bhattiprolu inscription (one PYQ-book explanation cites Naneghat, which is not an option here). The Allahabad pillar is Samudragupta's, Hathigumpha is Kharavela's, and Junagadh is Rudradaman's.

The NextGenIAS 2026 overlay that maps the Deccan-Roman routes (Ujjain-Paithan-Tagara-Bharuch) credits the ship coins to Vasishthiputra Pulumavi. Other notes also link ship-with-anchor coins to Yajna Sri Satakarni, but in this route context the answer is Vasishthiputra Pulumavi; Simuka and Gautamiputra are not credited with ship coins.
